issues.description: Function name mismatch for the sphere intersection API: example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h declares check_sphere_hit(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); but the implementation in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp defines bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) and callers in example_program/src/main.cpp invoke ray_sphere_intersect(...). The header, implementation and call sites use different identifiers, causing compilation errors (call sites include the header, so ray_sphere_intersect is undeclared) and confusing students about the intended API.

The sphere-intersection function is declared with a different identifier in the template header than it is implemented and used. In template/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h the function is declared as check_sphere_hit(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); whereas the implementation in template/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp defines ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) and calls in template/example_program/src/main.cpp also call ray_sphere_intersect(...). The solution repository header (solution/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h) uses ray_sphere_intersect as well. This mismatch (check_sphere_hit vs ray_sphere_intersect) prevents a clear mapping between declaration, implementation and use, causing compile-time confusion or linker issues and additional cognitive load for students trying to follow or modify the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the header declaration with the implementation and call sites. Replace the declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h with: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); This matches the .cpp implementation and usage in main.cpp (and the solution repository).
